scene.speaker: erik
scene.bubble: Jungle documentary night! Sofia knows every animal — and I brought popcorn for scientific reasons.
scene.intro: Jungle documentary night at the club house! Sofía knows every animal on the screen: the monkeys are noisy, the snake is long and quiet, the crocodile is dangerous and the elephant is enormous but gentle. Erik takes notes for a new invention: a camera that hangs from a tree. What lives in the jungle? Watch, listen and describe every animal!

activities.title: Read the sentences and write the jungle animals.

words.clue: It climbs trees and loves bananas.
Long, with no legs. It says sss!
A big orange cat with black stripes.
Long, green, with big teeth. It swims in rivers.
The biggest land animal, with a long nose.
A hot forest full of wild animals.

activities.title: Match the animal with where it hides.
Listen to the documentary. Write a word or number in each gap.

data.voice_note: Voces: Sofía (narradora de documental) y Erik (público con palomitas).
data.script: Sofia: Welcome to the jungle, the loudest place on Earth! … Sofia: The monkeys wake up first, at five in the morning. … Erik: Like my little brother! … Sofia: The tiger sleeps sixteen hours and hunts at night. … Sofia: The crocodile can wait in the water for two hours without moving. … Erik: Patience level: maximum. … Sofia: And the elephant family walks ten kilometres every day to find water. … Sofia: The jungle rule: everyone has a place, everyone has a job. … Erik: Beautiful! More popcorn?

data.text: Jungle guide: take your partner on an imaginary jungle walk. Point and describe 4 animals: "Look! A snake is hiding under…" Whisper — don't wake the tiger!

activities.title: Two pictures, many differences!
activities.instructions: Look at picture A and picture B. Find the 12 differences and tell your partner about them.

homework.prompt: Choose 3 jungle animals and write 2 sentences about each: where it lives, what it can do.

outcomes.puede: Understand longer dialogues (Movers parts 1–5); identify specific info in spoken texts.
Describe places, objects, past events; role-play simple situations.
Read and sequence short stories; locate information in signs, notices.
Write a note/message of 30–40 words (Movers Writing part); classroom paragraphs 60–100w.
~1350 words (Movers wordlist); Past simple, relatives, infinitive of purpose, have to.
